rows.question: Go through every project won in the last 12 to 24 months in your CRM or invoices and note for each how the client first found you (referral, walk-in, in-person pitch, event, website, repeat client); what share depended on meeting in person or on the office location?
rows.note: Asks what share of won projects depended on in-person meetings at the office; answer states most began in studio workshops.

rows.question: Ask your two or three largest clients directly, with a concrete question: would you still run workshops and sign-offs with us by video only, and would you consider moving work to an agency with its own premises?
rows.note: Asks clients about future video-only workshops; does not state where past projects started.

rows.question: Ask each team member privately (not in a group survey): would you want to work fully remote five days a week, and what does your home workspace look like? Include juniors and quieter members.
rows.note: Team preferences; none of the facts.

rows.question: Run a trial of one to two months with no one in the office on the usual shared days: what happens to review turnaround, the number of rework rounds and client feedback compared with the two previous months?
rows.note: Trial outcomes on turnaround and feedback; none of the facts.

rows.question: How do your junior designers currently get feedback and learn: write down how many hours per week they spend sitting with seniors, and decide what concrete replacement (scheduled pairing, review sessions) would cover it remotely.
rows.note: Junior mentoring; none of the facts.

rows.question: Have an accountant or payroll advisor check where each employee lives and works and which payroll, insurance, equipment and tax obligations fully remote work would trigger; what is the yearly cost?
rows.note: Payroll and tax obligations; none of the facts.

rows.question: Add up the costs the quarter-saving figure leaves out: home-office stipends, co-working or meeting room bookings for client workshops, software, equipment shipping and insurance; what is the net saving after them?
rows.note: Hidden remote costs; workshop room bookings do not state past workshop share.

rows.question: Ask the landlord whether a shorter lease, a smaller space, or a break clause is available, and check what comparable offices in the area would cost and how fast they are available if you needed to return.
rows.note: Asks how fast comparable offices are available to return; answer states they are booked out for years.

rows.question: Look at your last three hires or candidate pipelines: how many asked about the office, and how would you onboard a junior remotely? Ask two recruiters or peer studios what remote candidates in your field expect.
rows.note: Hiring and onboarding; none of the facts.

rows.question: Can you test a cheaper middle option, such as a smaller office or a co-working desk package with a meeting room for four weeks, to see how client meetings and walk-in leads change?
rows.note: Middle-option test; none of the facts.
